newsitem.title: INDIA: Classic Share's India cement stock recommendations.
newsitem.headline: Classic Share's India cement stock recommendations.

text.p: Classic Share & Stock Broking Services said it recommended investment in shares of select cement firms in India's cement deficit southern region.
"An investment exposure on units located in regions with long-term structural advantages will give good returns," Classic Share analyst Sriram Jitendra said in a sector report.
"With stocks currently trading at multiples well below their historic discountings, attractive valuations are available,' the report said.
It recommended investors to "buy" Madras Cements and Chettinad Cement Corpo and "accumulate" shares of India Cements and Dalmia Cement.

Classic said Madras Cements would post strong earnings growth while Chettinad would show moderate earnings growth. India Cements would show good earnings growth over a three-year horizon, the study forecast.
"Our analysis shows that units located along the Tamil Nadu-Kerala border and coastal Tamil Nadu will continue to do well even in the future," it said.
Cement firms based in the southern part of Andhra Pradesh state would perform well over the long term though their margins may come under pressure in the medium term, it said.
Cement firms in central Andhra Pradesh would have to regin themselves to low growth markets which offer poor realisations.
It said there was a wide disparity in cement prices between cement surplus and deficit areas in South India.

Presence of limestone deposits along a vein led to cement plants congregating close to these deposits. This resulted in skewed distribution of plants, forming pockets of cement surplus and deficit areas in southern India, the report said.
With freight costs being a crucial variable component of cost, this skewed distribution of plants resulted in different prices of cement across the region.
"Certain pockets are perpetually deficit in cement and therefore give a structural advantage to units catering to these markets," the report said.
